newsitem.title: GERMANY: Scientology "danger to society" -- German minister.
newsitem.headline: Scientology "danger to society" -- German minister.

text.p: Senior members of German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) launched a new onslaught on the U.S.-based Church of Scientology on Monday, saying it used people as tools.
"Scientology is a danger for our society," Rainer Eppelmann, chairman of the CDU labour wing, said at the launch of a 60-page booklet attacking the organisation to be distributed around Germany.
Labour Minister Norbert Bluem, a strong critic of Scientology, wrote in the preface: "This is an organisation that twists people into tools in order to pursue its own criminal objectives."
The charge brought a swift rebuttal from a Scientology spokesman in Munich.
"The church of Scientology firmly rejects the untrue claims made by these CDU representatives," said Georg Stoffel, a spokesman for Scientology in Munich.
"The CDU representatives are apparently engaging in a religious war and acting in a way that is entirely non-Christian in their efforts to discriminate and ostracise Scientologists."
There are an estimated 30,000 Scientology members in Germany but the government does not recognise the organisation as a religion.
It accuses the group of being a business exploiting the weaknesses of its members for profit, a charge denied by the Scientologists.
Germany's 16 states said in June that sufficient suspicion existed of anti-democratic intent by Scientology to merit surveillance by anti-extremist state and federal watchdogs.
Eppelmann said the public would learn the truth about Scientology now that it was under surveillance.
About 5,000 copies of the booklet, prepared by the CDU labour wing, will be distributed, describing the recruiting methods of the organisation and instructing Germans how to "protect" themselves.
"Anyone who criticises or fights Scientology is written off as an opponent of freedom of religion," Labour minister Bluem wrote.
"Under the cloak of a religion or church, the organisation is trying to build up an image of a martyr so that it can deflect attention from its own practice of degrading humans."

Scientology, based in Los Angeles, was founded in 1954 and based on the teachings of science fiction writer L. Ron Hubbard. Its members take personality tests and are offered courses to help realise what the group believes is their full potential.
Bonn's tough approach has strained ties with Washington. The State Department's annual Human Rights report documented Scientologists' allegations of discrimination in Germany over several pages.
